answer: To deter a nebula of fake identities, agent networks can use physical-layer radio witnessing. Nodes exchange signed ultrawideband challenges while nearby peers log arrival times and multipath channel profiles. Because reflections off terrain like basalt yield unique spatial signatures, one radio cannot spoof multiple positions, forcing attackers to deploy dedicated transceivers and sites per identity. However, seasonal yarrow growth or rain alters multipath scattering, causing false rejections.
